title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for CKD and T2DM.

HPI: Pt is a 90-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up of chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes. Pt reports feeling well today. Denies any acute shortness of breath, chest pain, or changes in urinary output. He continues to manage his glucose levels through diet alone. He reports adherence to low-sodium guidelines. No new complaints or concerns since last visit.

Medication List:
- Multivitamin daily
- Vitamin D3 supplement

Social History: Retired. Lives with wife. No tobacco use. Occasional alcohol.

Family History: Father had history of CKD. Mother had history of stroke.

Review of Systems:
General: No fatigue, no weight changes.
CV: No chest pain, no palpitations.
Resp: No SOB, no cough.
GI: No nausea, no diarrhea.
MSK: No joint pain, no falls.
Neuro: No dizziness, no focal weakness.

Vitals:
BP: 128/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs:
eGFR: 52 mL/min/1.73m2
HbA1c: 6.8%
BMP: Na+ 138, K+ 4.5, Cr 1.8

Exam:
Gen: Alert, oriented x3, well-appearing for age.
CV: RRR, S1, S2, no murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB.
Ext: WNL, no edema.

Assessment:
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 3a.
2. Type 2 diabetes.

Plan:
- Continue current diet-based management for T2DM.
- Continue monitoring of renal function.
- Follow up in 3 months for repeat labs and blood pressure check.
- Encouraged continued hydration and balanced diet.

Electronically signed, 
L. Moreau, DO
May 14, 2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.31.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
